page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance based on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture, running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. The server is powered by an AWS Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, provisioning 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core. Memory allocation stands at 16 GB, representing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. In addition to core compute and memory, the hardware configuration includes 237 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. It contains no specialized GPU accelerators.

Synthetic benchmarks show mid-tier memory handling alongside modest raw compute metrics. In memory tests, the instance records 63.9 GB/sec read and 30.56 GB/sec write throughput for large uncached blocks, sitting within average spectrums. However, cached small-block bandwidth is comparatively constrained at 236.33 GB/sec. Computational metrics reflect lower-tier performance in compute-heavy tasks: stress-ng single-core reaches 1520.19, while multi-core achieves 6055.75. Geekbench yields 921.0 in single-core and 3117.0 in multi-core routines. Database tests via PassMark show solid performance at 2648.72 operations, alongside 4.53 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations.

From an efficiency standpoint, the m6gd.xlarge leverages ARM-based power characteristics to offer economical operation for standard general-purpose profiles. The included 237 GB NVMe SSD avoids external storage overhead for temporary state, staging spaces, and local caches. The primary performance tradeoffs include limited single-threaded compute density and reduced instruction capabilities, lacking x86 vector extensions. Consequently, this server is suitable for intermediate database operations, caching nodes, continuous integration workers, and containerized backend services that benefit from fast local storage without requiring high floating-point compute.
description: Amazon Web Services m6gd.xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N1 architecture on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It integrates 4 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 16 GB of system RAM to provide a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. A key architectural distinction is its integrated 237 GB NVMe SSD local instance storage, providing fast temporary disk operations alongside 1 Gbps baseline network throughput. Performance testing indicates modest computational scores, with Geekbench single-core at 921.0 and multi-core at 3117.0, while PassMark database operations and large-block memory read bandwidth show steady mid-tier capability. Lacking dedicated graphics hardware and high-end compute acceleration, the m6gd.xlarge targets cost-efficient utility over compute intensity. It is primarily suited for containerized microservices, mid-tier relational databases, caching layers, and web application environments where bundled low-latency local storage adds operational value.
